arxiv-2009-14463.title: Neural RST-based Evaluation of Discourse Coherence
arxiv-2009-14463.creator: Grigorii Guz, Peyman Bateni, Darius Muglich, Giuseppe Carenini, University of British Columbia, Inverted AI {g.guz@cs, pbateni@cs, darius.muglich@alumni, carenini@cs}.ubc.ca
arxiv-2009-14463.description: Abstract This paper evaluates the utility of Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) trees and relations in discourse coherence evaluation. We show that incorporating silver-standard RST features can increase accuracy when classifying coherence. We demonstrate this through our tree-recursive neural model, namely RST-Recursive, which takes advantage of the text’s RST features produced by a state of the art RST parser.

arxiv-2012-06594.title: On the characteristics of fast neutrino flavor instabilities in three-dimensional core-collapse supernova models
arxiv-2012-06594.creator: Sajad Abbar, Francesco Capozzi, Robert Glas, H.-Thomas Janka, Irene Tamborra
arxiv-2012-06594.description: Abstract We assess the occurrence of fast neutrino flavor instabilities in two three-dimensional state-of-the-art core-collapse supernova simulations performed using a two-moment three-species neutrino transport scheme: one with an exploding 9 M ⊙ \mathrm{M_{\odot}} and one with a non-exploding 20 M ⊙ \mathrm{M_{\odot}} model.

arxiv-2105-03695.title: LPVcore: MATLAB Toolbox for LPV Modelling, Identification and Control This work has received funding from the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme (grant agreement nr. 714663).
arxiv-2105-03695.creator: Pascal den Boef, Pepijn B. Cox, Roland Tóth
arxiv-2105-03695.description: Abstract This paper describes the LPVcore software package for MATLAB developed to model, simulate, estimate and control systems via linear parameter-varying (LPV) input-output (IO), state-space (SS) and linear fractional (LFR) representations. In the LPVcore toolbox, basis affine parameter-varying matrix functions are implemented to enable users to represent LPV systems in a global setting, i.e., for time-varying scheduling trajectories.

arxiv-2109-01510.title: Safety-aware Motion Prediction with Unseen Vehicles for Autonomous Driving
arxiv-2109-01510.creator: Xuanchi Ren, Tao Yang, Li Erran Li, Alexandre Alahi, Qifeng Chen
arxiv-2109-01510.description: Abstract Motion prediction of vehicles is critical but challenging due to the uncertainties in complex environments and the limited visibility caused by occlusions and limited sensor ranges. In this paper, we study a new task, safety-aware motion prediction with unseen vehicles for autonomous driving.

arxiv-2303-17306.title: Constructions and equivalence of Sidon spaces
arxiv-2303-17306.creator: Chiara Castello, Olga Polverino, Paolo Santonastaso, Ferdinando Zullo
arxiv-2303-17306.description: Abstract Sidon spaces have been introduced by Bachoc, Serra and Zémor in 2017 as the q q -analogue of Sidon sets. The interest on Sidon spaces has increased quickly, especially after the work of Roth, Raviv and Tamo in 2018, in which they highlighted the correspondence between Sidon spaces and cyclic subspace codes.

arxiv-2304-09247.title: SigSegment: A Signal-Based Segmentation Algorithm for Identifying Anomalous Driving Behaviours in Naturalistic Driving Videos
arxiv-2304-09247.creator: Kelvin Kwakye & Younho Seong, Armstrong Aboah, Sun Yi
arxiv-2304-09247.description: Abstract In recent years, distracted driving has garnered considerable attention as it continues to pose a significant threat to public safety on the roads. This has increased the need for innovative solutions that can identify and eliminate distracted driving behavior before it results in fatal accidents.

arxiv-2304-14836.title: Training Large Scale Polynomial CNNs for E2E Inference over Homomorphic Encryption
arxiv-2304-14836.creator: Moran Baruch, Nir Drucker, Gilad Ezov, Yoav Goldberg, Eyal Kushnir, Jenny Lerner, Omri Soceanu, Itamar Zimerman
arxiv-2304-14836.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Moran Baruch, Nir Drucker, Gilad Ezov, Yoav Goldberg, Eyal Kushnir, Jenny Lerner, Omri Soceanu, Itamar Zimerman. Training large-scale CNNs that during inference can be run under Homomorphic Encryption (HE) is challenging due to the need to use only polynomial operations. This limits HE-based solutions adoption. We address this challenge and pioneer in providing a novel training method for large polynomial CNNs such as ResNet-152 and ConvNeXt models, and achieve promising accuracy on encrypted samples on large-scale dataset such as ImageNet.

arxiv-2308-02035.title: What Twitter Data Tell Us about the Future? Conference: ACM International Conference on Information Technology for Social Good; September 6–8, 2023; Lisbon, Portugal ACM International Conference on Information Technology for Social Good (GoodIT ’23), September 6–8, 2023, Lisbon, Portugal DOI: 10.114
arxiv-2308-02035.creator: Alina Landowska, Marek Robak, Maciej Skórski
arxiv-2308-02035.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Alina Landowska, Marek Robak, Maciej Skórski. Anticipation is a fundamental human cognitive ability that involves thinking about and living towards the future. While language markers reflect anticipatory thinking, research on anticipation from the perspective of natural language processing is limited. This study aims to investigate the futures projected by futurists on Twitter and explore the impact of language cues on anticipatory thinking among social media users.

arxiv-2404-13427.title: A Hilbert-Schmidt integral operator and the Weil distribution
arxiv-2404-13427.creator: Xian-Jin Li
arxiv-2404-13427.description: Abstract In this paper, a positive operator is given. It is shown that the product of this positive operator and the convolution operator is a trace class Hilbert-Schmidt integral operator and has nonnegative eigenvalues. A formula is given for the trace of this product operator.

arxiv-2405-17268.title: Suppressing defection by increasing temptation: the impact of smart cooperators on a social dilemma situation Journal: Applied Mathematics and Computation
arxiv-2405-17268.creator: Hsuan-Wei Lee, Colin Cleveland, and Attila Szolnoki
arxiv-2405-17268.description: Abstract In a social dilemma situation, where individual and collective interests are in conflict, it sounds a reasonable assumption that the presence of super or smart players, who simultaneously punish defection and reward cooperation without allowing exploitation, could solve the basic problem. The behavior of such a multi-strategy system, however, is more subtle than it is firstly anticipated.

arxiv-2504-06675.title: Probability Density Geodesics in Image Diffusion Latent Space
arxiv-2504-06675.creator: Qingtao Yu, Jaskirat Singh, Zhaoyuan Yang, Peter Henry Tu, Jing Zhang, Hongdong Li, Richard Hartley, Dylan Campbell
arxiv-2504-06675.description: Abstract Diffusion models indirectly estimate the probability density over a data space, which can be used to study its structure. In this work, we show that geodesics can be computed in diffusion latent space, where the norm induced by the spatially-varying inner product is inversely proportional to the probability density.

arxiv-2506-01063.title: AI4Contracts: LLM & RAG-Powered Encoding of Financial Derivative Contracts
arxiv-2506-01063.creator: Maruf Ahmed Mridul, Ian Sloyan, Aparna Gupta, Oshani Seneviratne
arxiv-2506-01063.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) are reshaping how AI systems extract and organize information from unstructured text. A key challenge is designing AI methods that can incrementally extract, structure, and validate information while preserving hierarchical and contextual relationships. We introduce CDMizer , a template-driven, LLM, and RAG-based framework for structured text transformation.

arxiv-2508-01300.title: How Far Are LLMs from Symbolic Planners? An NLP-Based Perspective
arxiv-2508-01300.creator: Ma’ayan Armony, Albert Meroño-Peñuela, Gerard Canal
arxiv-2508-01300.description: Abstract The reasoning and planning abilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) have been a frequent topic of discussion in recent years. Their ability to take unstructured planning problems as input has made LLMs’ integration into AI planning an area of interest. Nevertheless, LLMs are still not reliable as planners, with the generated plans often containing mistaken or hallucinated actions.

pmc-11458922.title: Uterine window and placenta accreta spectrum in a dichorionic, diamniotic twin gestation complicated by postpartum hemorrhage
pmc-11458922.creator: Ishwarya Sivakumar, Marika Toscano, Erin Gomez
pmc-11458922.description: Cesarean scar defects encompass a spectrum of separation of the uterine layers that increase risk of uterine rupture during labor and delivery. When coupled with the presence of placenta accreta spectrum, a condition characterized by abnormal adherence to or invasion of the myometrium by the placenta, the risk of life-threatening hemorrhage significantly increases.

pmc-11495208.title: The Clareon Vs AcrySof PanOptix Trifocal IOL: A Comparative Study of Patient Satisfaction and Visual Performance
pmc-11495208.creator: John A Hovanesian, Michael Jones, Quentin Allen
pmc-11495208.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeTo evaluate patient-reported outcomes of cataract surgery using the Clareon Panoptix and Panoptix Toric trifocal lenses and to compare these to the data collected previously for the AcrySof Panoptix and Panoptix Toric.Patients and MethodsProspective, open-label, multicenter analysis of satisfaction, spectacle independence, presence of unwanted side effects, and best-corrected visual acuity among patients undergoing cataract surgery who had been implanted at least 1 month previously with the Clareon PanOptix or PanOptix Toric trifocal IOL bilaterally.

pmc-11626536.title: Attachment State of Mind and complex traumatization in patients with Functional Motor Disorder (Motor Conversion Disorder)
pmc-11626536.creator: Cristina Civilotti, Veronica Nisticò, Roberta Tedesco, Sofia Cuoco, Rossella Bisogno, Paolo Barone, Alessia Celeghin, Giulia Di Fini, Gabriella Gandino, Roberto Erro, Benedetta Demartini
pmc-11626536.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionFunctional Motor Disorder (FMD) is characterized by motor neurological symptoms that cannot be explained by typical neurological diseases or other medical conditions. The role of psychological factors in the development, severity, and persistence of FMD remains unclear.

pmc-12375547.title: Review on Current Research on Biosynthesis of Biosurfactants and the Regulation Influenced by Metal Ions
pmc-12375547.creator: Yuchen Wang, Shan Qiao, Yongwu Niu
pmc-12375547.description: Biosurfactants, amphiphilic secondary metabolites mainly produced by microorganisms, can be categorized into five groups according to their chemical structure and source: glycolipids, lipopeptides, phospholipids, polymeric biosurfactants, and particulate surfactants. The hydrophobic segments of biosurfactants typically contain fatty acids of varying chain lengths, while their hydrophilic portions display a wide range of diversity. Diverse biosurfactants have distinct metabolic pathways.

pmc-12671074.title: Mapping bacterial microbiota variations in raw milk: geographic and type-specific insights
pmc-12671074.creator: Yujing Wang, Bowen Li, Rongbo Fan, Qijing Du, Dengpan Bu, Changjiang Zang, Jun Wang, Rongwei Han, Yongxin Yang
pmc-12671074.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Milk harbors a diverse array of microorganisms; however, the current understanding of the microbial diversity in raw milk from specific geographical origins and milk types remains unclear. To address this knowledge gap, this study employed single-molecule real-time sequencing to analyze the differences in microbial communities across various farms and milk types from different regions, specifically by examining the microbial diversity in Holstein cow milk samples from farms situated in both adjacent and distant regions, and comparing the microbial diversity between Holstein cow

pmc-12686421.title: Mitochondrial damage drives T-cell immunometabolic paralysis after major surgery
pmc-12686421.creator: Simon Hirschberger, Martin B Müller, Hannah Mascolo, Melissa Seitz, Stefan Nibler, David Effinger, Kun Lu, Joscha Büch, Martin Bender, Tobias Kammerer, Sven Peterß, Karin Kleigrewe, Miriam Abele, Teresa Barth, Olga Kushnir, Axel Imhof, Steffen Dietzel, Bernd Wegener, Ralf Sowa, Frank Vogel, Peter La
pmc-12686421.description: Cytotoxic T cell (CTL) dysfunction is a hallmark of immune paralysis after major surgery, increasing susceptibility to severe nosocomial infections and contributing to mortality in critically ill patients. The mechanisms remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that reactive oxygen species (ROS) released by myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSC) transiently emerging after surgery, drive perioperative CTL immunoparalysis.

pmc-13154512.title: Large-sized grafts versus standard-sized grafts combined with anterolateral ligament reconstruction in ACL-deficient knees: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13154512.creator: Mohamed Ali, Omar Abdelkarim, Yasser Soroor, Wael Salama, Moustafa Elsayed, Hossam El-Azab
pmc-13154512.description: BackgroundAnterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries are highly prevalent among athletes and continue to pose challenges owing to persistent instability and variable return-to-sport outcomes following reconstruction. Anterolateral ligament (ALL) reconstruction and has been introduced to improve outcomes. Increasing graft diameter was described to enhance biomechanical properties.

pmc-13299086.title: A Comprehensive Bioinformatic Analysis of SLC52A3 as a Prognostic Biomarker and Potential Therapeutic Target in Gynecological Cancers
pmc-13299086.creator: Monia Cecati, Valentina Schiavoni, Roberto Campagna, Giovanni Tossetta
pmc-13299086.description: Background/Objectives: The gene solute carrier family 52 member 3 (SLC52A3) encodes riboflavin transporter-3, a transmembrane protein essential for riboflavin absorption. Emerging evidence suggests that metabolic transporters may play a role in tumor biology. This study aimed to investigate the expression patterns, prognostic significance, genetic alterations, and functional associations of SLC52A3 in gynecological cancers.

pmc-13608804.title: Pan-Genome-Scale Metabolic Reconstruction Reveals Conserved Metabolic Functions in Candida albicans
pmc-13608804.creator: Ya Meng, Yiming Zhang, Lei Zhang
pmc-13608804.description: Candida albicans is a major cause of human mucosal and invasive fungal infections, but the relationship between its intraspecific genomic diversity and metabolic variation remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated 80 public C. albicans genome assemblies, published fungal genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs), public reaction databases, and orthogroup-linked gene–protein–reaction (GPR) evidence to construct a species-level C.
